necessary_context.content: On R^d, F(x)=f(x)+psi(x), f(x)=(1/n)sum_i f_i(x). Every f_i is convex and smooth; psi is convex, lower semicontinuous and possibly nonsmooth. x* is a minimizer. Theorem 2.1 requires each f_i to be L-smooth and psi to be sigma-strongly convex.
necessary_context.name: Problem (1.1)

necessary_context.content: Except Section 6 the norm is Euclidean. L-smoothness means ||grad h(x)-grad h(y)||<=L||x-y|| for all x,y. sigma-strong convexity means h(y)>=h(x)+<g,y-x>+(sigma/2)||x-y||^2 for the relevant subgradient g.
necessary_context.name: Euclidean smoothness and strong convexity

necessary_context.applies_to: Selected Option I implementation and performance
necessary_context.content: Algorithm 1 Option I has two exact proximal minimizations per inner iteration, at scales alpha and 1/(3L). The 1.5 amortized component-gradient count requires caching all n snapshot gradients, costing O(nd) storage in general; without caching the count is 2.5. Proximal operations are separately charged.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.9 Algorithm 1 lines 10–11, Remark 2.2 and footnote 11; p.10 continuation
necessary_context.name: Exact proximal operations and resource accounting
